page: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is a general purpose virtual machine in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU powered by an AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of RAM, 30 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute efficiency alongside capacity limitations inherent to a single-core profile. In stress-ng single-core tests, the dedicated EPYC core achieves performance within the top 25 percent of instances, mirrored by an average Geekbench single-core score of 1813.0. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also maintain average throughput at 28.4 GB/sec and 12.8 GB/sec respectively. However, total system throughput in multi-core benchmarks such as Geekbench multi-core (1789.0) and PassMark CPU (2647.82) falls in the bottom decile due to the single-thread limit. Memory subsystem testing shows large block read speeds of 31.44 GB/sec and write speeds of 22.58 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom quartile.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute availability without the noisy-neighbor interference common in burstable tiers. The bundled NVMe SSD provides low latency for local storage operations, though the 30 GB capacity restricts the scale of resident data. This configuration delivers high cost efficiency for workloads that require reliable single-threaded execution without paying for surplus cores. Best-fit operational environments include lightweight microservices, background job workers, API gateway endpoints, monitoring agents, and staging servers.
description: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is an entry-level general purpose instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 1 dedicated AMD EPYC core at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 30 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage on the x86_64 architecture. Without GPU acceleration, the server focuses on dependable baseline computing, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI extensions. In benchmark evaluations, the dedicated core yields strong stress-ng single-core output and average Geekbench single-core responsiveness, though overall throughput in multi-threaded benchmarks, database operations, and memory bandwidth is strictly constrained by the single-thread architecture. The dedicated resource assignment eliminates virtualization contention found in shared-core instances while keeping infrastructure overhead low. This instance is appropriate for running low-traffic web applications, background worker queues, monitoring agents, lightweight API services, and basic development sandboxes requiring predictable execution.
